original_question: Construct a holomorphic minimal foliation, or a holomorphic minimal lamination, on a compact complex manifold that has uncountably many mutually singular extremal directed currents which are ddc-closed but not closed.
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 7.1, “Foliations with many directed harmonic currents”: the open problem asking for a holomorphic minimal foliation or lamination on a compact complex manifold with uncountably many extremal directed dd^c-closed currents that are not closed. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct ambient geometric setting from the paper—holomorphic minimal foliation/lamination on a compact complex manifold—and the central requirement of uncountably many extremal directed currents that are dd^c-closed but not closed. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
missing_details: The paper’s formulation is about positive directed currents; positivity is implicit in the surrounding setup and should be stated explicitly in a stand-alone question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
“Directed” should be tied explicitly to the foliation/lamination, since Section 1 defines directed currents in that sense. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
Minimality should be unpacked: immediately before Problem 7.1 the paper says that minimal means every leaf is dense. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

For stand-alone use, “ddc-closed” should be corrected to “dd^c-closed,” and the operator should be identified as dd^c=(i/π)∂∂̄; the introduction gives this notation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The ambient currents in this paper are those naturally associated with foliations/laminations by Riemann surfaces, i.e. positive currents of bidimension (1,1); that context is omitted in the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The phrase “mutually singular” is not part of the official statement of Problem 7.1. It appears only in the preceding motivating example of Fornæss-Sibony-Wold for closed currents, so keeping it would strengthen and slightly shift the paper’s actual open problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
refined_question: Construct a holomorphic minimal foliation (respectively, a holomorphic minimal lamination) by Riemann surfaces on a compact complex manifold that carries uncountably many extremal positive dd^c-closed currents of bidimension (1,1), directed by the foliation (respectively, lamination), such that none of these currents is closed; here minimal means that every leaf is dense, and dd^c=(i/π)∂∂̄. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
justification: This is the exact nearest official formulation in the paper because Section 7 is the only place where all of the distinctive ingredients of your draft occur together: minimal foliation/lamination, compact complex manifold, uncountably many extremal directed currents, and the requirement dd^c-closed but not closed. The immediately preceding sentence explains where your added phrase “mutually singular” came from: it recalls the Fornæss-Sibony-Wold example of a compact minimal lamination with uncountably many mutually singular extremal directed closed currents, which serves as motivation for Problem 7.1 but is not itself part of the formal open problem. Section 1 supplies the notation dd^c and the notion of a directed current. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
